claims.text: The alloy is a multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy with distinct phase boundaries.
Protective oxide films naturally form on the alloy.
Mechanical wear disrupts or removes protective oxide films at eutectic phase boundaries.
Disruption of the oxide films exposes vulnerable underlying phases or material.
The newly exposed material undergoes accelerated localized corrosion.
Corrosion of the exposed material produces abrasive corrosion by-products.
Abrasive corrosion by-products further intensify mechanical wear.
Reciprocal enhancement of corrosion and wear creates a positive feedback loop.
The positive feedback loop causes synergistically accelerated total degradation relative to isolated wear and isolated corrosion.
Elevated temperature enhances corrosion kinetics under the proposed exposure conditions.
Elevated temperature enhances wear damage under the proposed exposure conditions.
Simultaneous wear-corrosion will produce degradation exceeding the additive effects measured in isolated wear and isolated corrosion tests.
Simultaneous wear-corrosion will produce greater total weight loss than the isolated-exposure baselines.
Simultaneous wear-corrosion will produce deeper wear tracks than the isolated wear baseline.
Simultaneous wear-corrosion will produce more pronounced localized corrosion than the isolated corrosion baseline.
Enhancing oxide-film stability should reduce synergistic degradation during simultaneous wear-corrosion.
The proposed mechanism is most relevant to eutectic high-entropy alloys having distinct phase boundaries and protective oxide films.
